prereg_plan: Where a study has not calculated total screen time, calculate it as the sum of time spent on different devices or types.
deviation: Done as proposed, but only in the analysis. The harmonised total row holds dedicated items only, and the analysis derives a total: the dedicated item where one exists, otherwise a sum of activity rows that needs watching and gaming at minimum, never adds device rows to activity rows, and is capped at 24 hours.
reason: A sum of separately asked activities counts concurrent use twice, so it is not comparable with a directly reported total and should not be stored as one.
assessment: Summed totals still include concurrent use. Source and coverage are moderators, and sensitivity analyses use dedicated items only and exclude sums above 24 hours.

prereg_plan: Create a version of the dataset in March 2026 to be used for the analyses.
deviation: No version was created then. The specification and the datasets for the report to the funder are fixed at a freeze due on 20 November 2026, and the datasets for the publications in late January 2027. Each is recorded as a data manifest.
reason: Harmonisation took longer than planned, and contributors are still providing data.
assessment: The freeze still precedes the confirmatory models, which is what the preregistered version was for.

prereg_plan: An observational design with no manipulated variables.
deviation: Trials are included where the screen use measured could reasonably be considered ecologically valid. The analysis uses their baseline waves and control arms.
reason: These datasets measure everyday screen use as well as observational studies do, before or apart from any intervention.
assessment: Rows affected by an intervention are left out of the primary analysis; a sensitivity analysis adds all arms with an arm covariate.

prereg_plan: Eligible datasets have a mean sample age younger than 18 years.
deviation: Eligibility is decided row by row in the analysis: rows aged under 19 are kept, older rows and rows with no recorded age are dropped, and a dataset's mean age is not used.
reason: Some eligible datasets include adults or follow children into adulthood, and a strict under-18 rule would remove final-year school students.
assessment: The analysed sample matches the population the research questions are about more closely than a dataset-level rule would.

prereg_plan: Impute missing screen time, covariate and moderator data by multiple imputation by chained equations.
deviation: Imputation runs within each unit and fills sporadic missingness only. A variable a unit never measured stays missing and is handled by covariate tiers. Outcomes are used to impute but imputed outcome values are not analysed.
reason: A variable a study never measured cannot be imputed from that study's own data, and imputing it from other studies would borrow different instruments and populations.
assessment: Fewer values are imputed than the preregistration implies. The complete-case sensitivity analysis is kept.

deviation: 50 for confirmatory cells; fewer are allowed for rows that are reported but not tested.
assessment: Confirmatory results keep the preregistered number.

prereg_plan: Use Rubin's rules to combine the results from all imputed datasets.
deviation: Rubin's rules are used for slopes. Intervals for breakpoints come from a dataset-level bootstrap combined with imputation.
reason: Rubin's rules assume an estimate that is close to normally distributed, which a breakpoint is not.

prereg_plan: For the primary analyses, exclude data more than 3 absolute deviations from the median, and exclude implausible values.
deviation: Primary analyses exclude only implausible values: screen use above 24 hours a day and outcome values outside the dataschema's bounds. The 3-MAD rule runs as sensitivity analyses on screen use and on outcomes.
reason: Screen measures are mostly zero or banded, so the median absolute deviation is often zero and the rule flags every child who uses a screen; on symptom scales it removes the severe tail.
assessment: The preregistered rule is still run and reported, so a reader can see whether the departure changes any conclusion.

prereg_plan: Record the tool used to measure screen time and include it as a covariate.
deviation: Measure type and responder are moderators when results are pooled across datasets. The tool's name is reported but not modelled.
reason: The tool is the same for everyone in most datasets, so it cannot be a covariate within a dataset.
assessment: Differences between tools are still examined, at the level where they vary.

prereg_plan: Address the research questions using piecewise regression.
deviation: Tiers 1 and 2 estimate a linear slope per extra hour a day. Piecewise models are used in Tier 3, where the question is about thresholds.
reason: The Tier 1 and 2 hypotheses are about whether and in which direction screen use is associated with outcomes, which a single slope tests directly.
assessment: A linear slope summarises a relationship that may be curved; Tier 3 estimates the shape. An amendment to the registration states this.

prereg_plan: Test whether location of screen use (home or school) moderates the associations (RQ4).
deviation: Reported as insufficient evidence unless 3 or more datasets have matched school and any-location measures at the freeze.
reason: Very few datasets record screen use at school.
assessment: The hypothesis about location is likely to go untested, and the report says so.

prereg_plan: Contributors may share results through secure remote analysis (DataSHIELD).
deviation: Not used for now. All analyses run centrally on data the contributors provided. It may return in a later iteration.
reason: No contributor has needed it so far.
assessment: No dataset has been lost for want of this route.

prereg_plan: Registration prior to analysis of the data.
deviation: Rough correlations were produced and given only to the funder, and the analysis code is developed before the freeze on a short list of exposure and outcome cells: screen-based watching against the wellbeing family and against grade repetition (analysis/development_cells.csv). The report to the funder follows the freeze.
reason: The funder asked for early indications, and the code had to be developed on real data in the time available.
assessment: Analyses are not blinded. A tagged commit of the frozen specification before the full model list is run, and the public history, separate exploration from confirmation. Results for the development cells are marked as seen before the freeze wherever they are reported.

deviation: The analysis uses the dataschema's sex row, which holds sex or gender as each source recorded it.
reason: Most datasets record one binary variable and do not say which it is.
assessment: Results are described as differences by sex or gender as recorded.

prereg_plan: One version of the dataset for all analyses.
deviation: The frozen specification is run on the datasets available for the report to the funder, then re-run on the full set for the publications, after the report's results have been seen.
reason: Several groups provide data after the report is due.
assessment: More data for the publications. A dataset is included on its diagnostics alone, never on what it does to a result, and a reconciliation table shows every difference between the two runs.

prereg_plan: Not in the preregistration: risk of bias.
deviation: Each dataset is rated for risk of bias after the report to the funder, so after results have been seen. The rating is a moderator in the publications.
reason: Rating every dataset could not be done properly before the report.
assessment: The moderator's model is fixed at the freeze. Ratings made with results in view could be influenced by them.
